title: Enhancing Recombinant Protein Expression in Escherichia coli Using Ethanol
author: Chhetri, Kalita, et al.
materials: Lysis buffer (phosphate, Tris or PBS buffer of pH 8.0)

•High-grade sterile LB agar plates.•Ethanol (analytical or molecular biology grade).•Antibiotics (ampicillin, kanamycin, etc.).•IPTG stock solution (1 M) for protein induction (IPTG should be a filter sterilized).•Lysis buffer for pellet re-suspension. (Lysis buffer can be phosphate, Tris or PBS buffer of pH 8.0.)•Properly autoclaved culture vials/tubes for cell growth.•Shaking incubator for culture growth.•Cooling centrifuge for cell harvesting.•Spectrophotometer for monitoring cell growth.•Erlenmeyer flask of different size depending on the culture volume.Note: This list does not include any small generic laboratory equipments that are assumed to be available. Chemicals and other components can be used from any reliable company.•Choice of appropriate antibiotics depends on the vector construct and E. coli expression hosts.Note: Several other vectors and E. coli expression hosts are commercially available in the market; they can also be used for molecular cloning and protein expression as per the recommended protocol provided by manufacturers with appropriate selective antibiotics.

steps.title: Prepare starter culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony from the transformed LB agar plate (or use 20 µL glycerol stock) and inoculate into 5 mL LB broth containing the appropriate antibiotics for the vector/host.

steps.title: Grow overnight starter
steps.instruction: Incubate the starter culture at 37 °C with shaking at 180 rpm for 14–16 h.

steps.title: Set up experimental vials
steps.instruction: Label five 5 mL culture vials as: Control (un‑induced), Induced without ethanol, Induced with 1 % ethanol, Induced with 2 % ethanol, Induced with 3 % ethanol.

steps.title: Inoculate vials with starter
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of the overnight starter culture to each vial containing 5 mL LB medium with the same antibiotics.

steps.title: Add ethanol and grow to mid‑log
steps.instruction: To the three ethanol‑designated vials add ethanol to a final concentration of 1 % (v/v), 2 % (v/v) or 3 % (v/v) respectively; grow all vials at 37 °C with vigorous shaking for approximately 3–4 h until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.5–0.6. Note: 3 % ethanol gives maximal expression; concentrations >5 % inhibit growth.

steps.title: Induce protein expression with IPTG
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to each induced vial (including ethanol‑treated ones) to a final concentration of 1.0 mM. Do not add IPTG to the non‑induced control.

steps.title: Post‑induction incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the cultures after IPTG addition as follows:

substeps.instruction: Standard: 4–5 h at 37 °C with continuous shaking.
Optional low‑temperature: 20–22 h at 16–23 °C after induction (useful for solubility screening).
For auto‑induction media: incubate until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.4–0.6.

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of each culture into a micro‑centrifuge tube and spin at 12,000 rpm for 1 min. Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare lysates for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 60 µL of pH 8.0 buffer (Tris, phosphate or PBS), add 20 µL of 10 % SDS and 20 µL of 5× SDS loading dye, then mix/pipette to lyse.

steps.title: Heat‑denature samples
steps.instruction: Boil the lysates at 100 °C for 5–10 min, vortexing briefly between heating intervals.

steps.title: Perform SDS‑PAGE analysis
steps.instruction: Load the boiled samples onto an SDS‑polyacrylamide gel, run electrophoresis, and analyze protein expression levels.
